texts: A left aortic arch with an aberrant right subclavian artery is an incomplete ring: E.
The right subclavian artery arises last from the arch and passes behind the oesophagus, but with a left ligamentum nothing closes the circle, so it can only indent the oesophagus from behind.
A double aortic arch, whichever side is dominant, and a right arch with a retroesophageal left subclavian artery and a left ligamentum are complete rings round the trachea and oesophagus.
A right arch with mirror-image branching usually forms no ring at all.
In the picture, only the jester's shackle is left open.
Memory hook: the jester's trick never closes the ring.
